title: Joseph Forgives His Brothers
text:
Jacob loved his son Joseph more than his other sons and gave him a richly ornamented robe. Joseph told his brothers about dreams in which they bowed down to him. They hated him for it. One day, far from home, they seized him, threw him into a dry pit, and sold him to traders bound for Egypt. They dipped his robe in goat's blood and let their father believe a wild animal had killed him.

In Egypt, Joseph was a slave, then a prisoner, and finally, after interpreting Pharaoh's dreams, governor of the whole land, in charge of storing grain for a coming famine.

When the famine struck, his brothers came to Egypt to buy grain and bowed before him. They did not recognize him. Joseph tested them: he accused them of spying, kept one brother hostage, and demanded they bring the youngest, Benjamin. When they returned with him, Joseph had his silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack and declared that Benjamin would be his slave. Judah stepped forward and begged to be taken instead, because losing Benjamin would kill their father.

Joseph could no longer control himself. He sent everyone else out and wept so loudly the Egyptians heard. "I am Joseph," he said. He told them not to be distressed or angry with themselves: God had sent him ahead to save lives. He kissed his brothers and wept over them, and sent for his father Jacob to come to Egypt.
lesson: Forgiveness can follow even deep betrayal, especially when it meets real change in those who did wrong. Look for the change before you test, and then let the test end.
people: Joseph, his brothers, Judah, Benjamin, Jacob
